preamble: Palatalization (secondary palatalization or 'softening') raises the body of the tongue toward the hard palate during the articulation of a consonant, typically before front vowels or a palatal glide. It is phonemic in East Slavic languages such as Russian, automatic before front vowels in Lithuanian, and arises morphologically in Romanian, where plural -i surfaces as palatalization of a final consonant. It recurs across several Indo-European branches (Slavic, Baltic, Romance) and is among the most widespread secondary articulations cross-linguistically.

examples.note: 'eye(s)'; word-final non-syllabic -i realized as palatalization of k
